author: Doctor
text:
Chanya, the engulf has been well described by DharmaTrader. in particular the last large bearish candle with tail. A dead give away that buying came in and is at the moment even after the NY close looking bullish. The price action has been what I would expect to see when a trend sets up on lower time frames. An engulf is only of benefit when it appears in the right places. By now all will know the right place to look for a new move with price action are in the higher time frame supply and demand areas. The range which eur/usd is inside will once again get another rattle to see who has the money to bust it out and keep it going.

Vito, the candle you marked was my second entry point. It pushed briefly below near term demand and into previous demand and got extra orders, plus a nice false move to boot. Which when you think about it, anyone who went short there and got stopped out gave a dirt cheap long trade into pro money hands.

baltimore, I am glad you pulled out my old aussie chart, would ever would have thought price would go where I said it would. But if more traders would watch the snail rather than the rabbit i.e do not focus on the lower time frames, a lot more success would be achieved. The change in direction happens so slowly on the monthly that most traders wont see the change at all. Until one day the media pimp it, which will be after the fact. There is a ton of down side in that pair and good money to be made. Just look at all the fresh air between current price and historical price, nice!

joema, those ma initials still get me. How about joersi or joecci, hmmm nah. joema it has to be:) If you draw a line on 85850, can you see it is an S/R area?.....a great place for moves to come off of. But given the long bullish candles (2) that formed there, I was not going to chase price and let it go until it setup today. You are correct about the long tails, they are great emotional flags to get shorts coming in. But when you look at it as pro money does, its a great way to get shorts in and also a fast way to hit old demand and you get two birds with one stone and a ton of your money in the market at the cheapest prices all day. There was enough room for profit and an obvious target over head. Pro money know where all the stops are, its childs play to pull them out with a spike, most day traders stops wont be far from their entries and are put behind the last low (or high) or behind a swing. There is more profit to be had from getting people on the wrong side of the market than there is with taking out stops. If you get people trading the wrong way, you will get their stop and the few points they had gained. Thats more value than a stop alone.

Christian, the NZD/USD tends to follow AUD/USD and there is plenty down side in the NZD. It may take a little more time but my thoughts are for bearish entries on it. some early low value entries may well work out and step them down. Even though it is now after the NY close, the NZD will become active shortly. There is nice bearish action slowly coming in and the odd bull trying to push it higher. Supply has just been hit on the 5min and this is playing into old supply back on june 20th, we are just in that area now and any last bullish activity will be tested around here. On the daily we are below an S/R area which is good for the bears. On your last chart where you have the blue line, thats going to be the real test to see have the bears taken it.

Great posts from you all, and some real quality too.

author: Vito
text:
EUR/GBP EXERCISE

Another try at first entry of Doc's EUR/GBP trade.

1. We had a strong push down on H4 as seen on the chart. So we need to engulf the origin for further move up. Next H4 bar move up doesn't engulf it so we wait.

2. Later right at the edge of that bearish H4 bar we have large spikes on M15 getting above that origin but all of them closing below the edge of bearish H4 bar showing push down. a. if it was real time I would expect a price drop as I would see collecting orders for move down.

3. No strong move down happens. Instead we have a strong bullish M15 bar closing highest of those large spikes and also strongly closing above the bearish H4 bar's edge.

4. Price moves back down with a strong M15 bar but stops at previous bullish bar's demand. Later spikes into that demand and gets rejected finding support. That is the entry signal.

Or am I trying too hard?

author: Doctor
text:
Guys, thanks for your comments and input. As I see it the concept of posting educational material is a difficult task to get tuned correctly for traders of all levels. It means there is no known starting point because I have to try and cover all bases and I have no idea of the background and experience for any of you....not just those who replied of late, but of the wider readership.

Then there is the problem of building all the material which as you can imagine takes a long time and if it eats into my trading time, I just wont do it. In the past I stood before students and engaged their brains, I knew the knowledge level of all and it was a starting point from which I could build. To get everyone along the curve in trading, it too has to be provided with a time line and base from which all can proceed with the principles firmly implanted. I am know it must be frustrating for some of you to look at some of my trades and wonder, how did that work?

Getting the years of screen time from my head into yours is not an easy task and I cant do it in a matter of weeks or months. Trading takes a long time to understand and the time taken to learn must be compared to the time it takes to get a formal education. There is no such thing as formal trading qualifications and getting access to the right mind set is very important because you must be shown that what is being given to you is real and you can prove it for yourself over time.

Once you have a grounding in trading, you then build upon it over time. If I could get you all into a trading room and get new comers in first and show the big picture, then those people can move on to a level where a greater number of people will be comfortable. Then move to the next step up and so on. Unfortunately there are 24hrs between some of us and daily work and of course life in general to get in the way. Then I have a the trouble of not trading while teaching and knowing full well there is more money in trading than being a teacher it makes no financial sense.

It is in the little down time I get my posts appear here. There are times between trades or while I wait for a trade to finish when I can get some post together. Clearly there has to be some way to get people to progress which wont impact myself and still give you all quality material. If I had a buck for each time I got asked to write a book, make a course, start a signals service, produce live webinars or appear at live shows etc etc, I could make a living from that alone. But it is a different way of work and life and not a path I have taken.

Some time ago I mentioned I would start a blog and put info up on that and not make my journal all things to all men, which it can never be.

The most practical way for any of you to learn will be historical i.e printed material and videos. At a later stage it will be time spent live in the markets with a trader sitting next to you. Few will ever have that luxury. I really need to hear where you are technically, emotionally and financially. In other words, do you have any clue about trading and new to it, or not a new trader but struggling. Does your head throw a loop when you take a hit or the market reverse when your analysis said otherwise, and do you have enough money to trade, or are you trying to make this months rent from it?

If I can find some common traits I will look into getting something together, but no promises because time is indeed money and we all need to make some. I would also appreciate input on setting up a blog cos this guy knows nothing about websites or finding ways to get timely info onto one. I like the idea of posting comments about a pair as the market unfolds live. Perhaps this is too ambitious, but it would be a good learning tool.

In order to keep this thread clean, please send me an email where you need help and I will post back here with the results of where the most help is needed. Then I will see if its practical to get some new posts here to bring you along. I will give it two weeks to allow for summer holiday time etc before showing the results.

thedoctortrader@gmail.com

author: Doctor
text:
A chart of a recent short on GBP/USD. Price action and where it was at the time had setup a good place to short from, and the move down caught everyone by surprise with the force behind the move. It is at times like these you do not wait for a target to be hit, which as you can see was much lower than when I closed the trade as I took the screen pic.

These moves are unsustainable and no further sellers can help get price lower for a long time. If you look a few posts back you will also see a EUR/USD trade I took with a similar sharp move and I did not wait around waiting for an obvious target to be hit, it was just too risky and giving all those points back makes no sense.

This is where supply and demand have no effect. They do not always work because those two mentioned trades were based off supply and demand, but the targets could not possibly meet their targets. There comes a time when moves in the market do not behave in how you expect them to, and this must get your radar on alert and make preparations for getting out.

Last chart is EUR/USD long. We saw a nice shake out and took may by surprise. But if you waited for the longer term picture to unfold you got a very clear picture of where the Euro was going. I loaded up and letting it ride. The large move up I posted a while back never saw any decent price action to support it and no major players will to off load much, so we had to sit through much chop and false moves in an attempt to grab the orders the bulls wanted.

The only place of interest on the chart was the deep spike down onto the top of the old large move up. How nice of pro money to give themselves one massive ride up. Anyone who spotted this in real time, three cheers to you.....top trader.

author: Vito
text:
Hello all,

Since Doc is on vacation I hope my post here won't clouder the thread too much. I'm rereading Doc's thread and I catch myself not understanding the decision points Doc is explaining. So I hope somebody can explain this question I have here.

My understanding of decision points is when we have price near S/R and there is a clear strong break of that S/R area. The origin of that move is a decision point.

Now in few posts here I see some other PA called a decision point and I will quote part of Doc's post here to show it.

Doctor wrote: Here is the daily chart.

Box A carried over from the higher time frames and while its a good distance away, always keep it in mind as over head resistance as well as a target if longs look good. The blue line is also carried over and the purple too far down to see it on this time frame. The blue line now shows some order to the chaos, note the support it provided in the past, many hits, therefore it is of significance.

About the blue line is a black line, a lesser line of importance but still price has reacted here with both support and resistance coming in. It was the precursor to the last bullish move last week. Practically pixel perfect. Marked are two D candles, even though more exist, these are the most important that immediately jump out. These are decision candles where price decided it was time to make a move, note how it happens to also be at last Friday's close too, another decision area. Who would have guessed?
